title: Eventual properness for finite type algebraic spaces without finite presentation
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback to any affine scheme is affine. Locally finite type means that the ring maps on etale scheme charts have finitely many algebra generators. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$. Let $h_{i_0}:W_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ be a locally finite type morphism with $W_{i_0}$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $i\ge i_0$ put $W_i=W_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, and put $W=W_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. If $W\to T$ is proper, then $W_j\to T_j$ is proper for some $j\ge i_0$. Neither $h_{i_0}$ nor any transition map is assumed finitely presented or flat.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), in Situation (situation-descent-property), with B_i=Y_i=T_i and X_i=W_i; local finite type version, no finite-presentation assumption.

proof.text: Write $a=i_0$. Every $T_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since it is affine. Thus $h_a$ is quasi-compact by quasi-compact-source/quasi-separated-target permanence, and is of finite type by the assumed local finite type. The space $D_a=W_a\times_{T_a}W_a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the fibre-product permanence statement. The diagonal $\delta_a:W_a\to D_a$ is representable and locally of finite type, without a finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), separated-stage reduction; Tag 0851 (lemma-descend-separated-morphism), diagonal argument, using spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 073B and 03HK

proof.text: The base change of $\delta_a$ to $T$ is the diagonal of $W\to T$: on test objects both fibre squares consist of pairs of sections with equal image in the base. It is a closed immersion since $W\to T$ is proper. Apply [lem-sfb-space-descend-closed-immersion] to $W_a\to D_a$ over the affine base system. Its two spaces are qcqs and its morphism is locally of finite type by step 1. There is $b\ge a$ for which $\delta_b$ is a closed immersion, so $W_b\to T_b$ is separated.

Restrict to indices $i\ge b$. This is still a nonempty directed set. It has the same limit: for any original index $k$, choose an upper bound of $k,b$ and compose its cone map to $T_k$; a common upper bound shows independence of that choice and uniqueness. All $W_i$ are qcqs by fibre-product permanence applied to $W_a,T_i,T_a$. Local finite type persists by arbitrary base change, and $W_i\to T_i$ is quasi-compact by source/target permanence, hence finite type. For $i\ge b$ it is separated by base change from $W_b\to T_b$. Iterated fibre products identify $W_b\times_{T_b}T_i$ with $W_i$ and $W_b\times_{T_b}T$ with $W$, since both represent the same compatible tuples of sections.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), replacing 0 by a separated stage

proof.text: Apply weak Chow to the separated finite-type map $W_b\to T_b$, whose base is affine. It supplies an integer $n\ge0$, a quasi-compact separated scheme $C_b$, a proper universally surjective map $\pi_b:C_b\to W_b$, and a quasi-compact immersion $j_b:C_b\to P_b=\mathbf P^n_{T_b}$ with $q_bj_b=h_b\pi_b$. For $i\ge b$ and for the limit put $C_i=C_b\times_{T_b}T_i$ and $P_i=\mathbf P^n_{T_i}$, and likewise $C,P$ over $T$. The projective-space base-change convention identifies $P_i$ with $P_b\times_{T_b}T_i$; the maps $j_i$ are immersions by immersion base change. The maps $\pi_i$ and $\pi$ are proper by proper base change, and universally surjective by the universally-surjective clause of weak Chow and the associativity of fibre products.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), Chow diagram and its base changes; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow)

proof.text: At the limit $C\to W\to T$ is proper by composition. Since $C,T$ are schemes, the representable-proper scheme-test equivalence gives properness as a scheme morphism (take the identity test of $T$). The projection $q:P=\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ is proper, hence separated. Scheme proper-over-separated cancellation makes $j:C\to P$ proper, since $qj=C\to T$. It remains an immersion by step 4; a proper immersion of schemes is a closed immersion. Thus $j$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), the limit immersion is closed; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NX (lemma-universally-closed-permanence), (2)

proof.text: The scheme $C_b$ is quasi-compact and separated, so it is quasi-separated: apply separated-implies-quasi-separated to its structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The projection $P_b\to T_b$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated; since $T_b$ is qcqs, $P_b$ is qcqs by scheme qcqs permanence. The immersion $j_b$ is locally of finite type. Apply scheme closed-immersion descent to $j_b:C_b\to P_b$ over $(T_i)_{i\ge b}$, with limit base $T$. The stage base and both schemes are qcqs, and step 5 gives its closed limit base change. There is $c\ge b$ such that $j_c$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), final closed-immersion descent; limits.tex Tag 01ZP (lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation)

proof.text: The closed immersion $j_c$ is proper, and $q_c:P_c\to T_c$ is proper. Hence $p_c=q_cj_c:C_c\to T_c$ is a proper scheme morphism. It is also proper as a morphism of algebraic spaces: every scheme test is its scheme base change, proper by scheme proper base change, so the representable-proper test equivalence applies.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), properness of the closed projective stage

proof.text: For any algebraic-space map $B\to T_c$, the induced $\pi_B:C_c\times_{T_c}B\to W_c\times_{T_c}B$ is surjective by step 4. Its point map is continuous. If $F\subseteq|W_c\times_{T_c}B|$ is closed, then $\pi_B^{-1}(F)$ is closed and has closed image under the proper base change of $p_c$; surjectivity gives $h_B(F)=p_B(\pi_B^{-1}(F))$. Thus every $h_B$ is closed. The map $h_c$ is universally closed, and step 3 already gives that it is separated and of finite type. These are exactly the three clauses of properness, so $h_c$ is proper and $c\ge b\ge i_0$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_proper_stage_of_locallyOfFiniteType {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (haff : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffine (D.obj i).left) (htrans : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a).left) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I) (W₀ : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (h₀ : W₀ ⟶ schemeSpace (D.obj (op i₀))) (hqc : ∃ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ W₀.obj.obj), CompactSpace U.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (prod.lift (𝟙 W₀.obj.obj) (𝟙 W₀.obj.obj))) (hlft : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) h₀) (hproper : MapIsProper (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := schemeSpace c.pt) (Y := schemeSpace (D.obj (op i₀))) ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over _).yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i₀)))) h₀)) : ∃ (j : I) (hj : i₀ ≤ j), MapIsProper (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := schemeSpace (D.obj (op j))) (Y := schemeSpace (D.obj (op i₀))) ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over _).yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE hj).op))) h₀)
